Container.Name: Audiobind
Container.Overview: Finds audiobooks that are split into many files, checks each one against the Audible catalog, merges the parts into a single tagged m4b with real chapter marks and cover art, and files it as Author/Book/Book.m4b (or Author/Series/3 - Title/). Runs on a timer and only converts books it is confident about.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: audiobook m4b merge convert chapters metadata audible audnex audiobookshelf
Container.Changes:
### 0.21.0 * Backups are honest now that the database runs in WAL mode: copy with `sqlite3 audiobind.db ".backup copy.db"`, not by copying the file while the app runs * An encode can no longer leave a half-written book: publishing is atomic across filesystems, and the duration check catches a dropped file inside a long book * A re-save no longer wipes a book's match evidence, and a pinned book's cover is found again * The matcher stops trusting a single candidate: a window-only title match cannot reach MEDIUM, and an adaptation nobody asked for loses to the plain edition of the same book * A hand-set ASIN the catalog has no data for gives up after three checks instead of blocking the book forever
### 0.20.0 * Audio channels default to 2 (stereo); `AUDIO_CHANNELS=1` still halves the file size * The Series tab now shows a series you own a single book of, so you find the ones you did not know were series * Book rows look expandable and open from the keyboard (Tab, then Enter or Space) * The template pins a release tag instead of `:latest`, so an install is a build you can name
### 0.19.0 * New conversions follow the Audiobookshelf folder convention: `Author/Book/` or `Author/Series/3 - Title/`, with every author in the folder * Settings > Library: **Match Audiobookshelf layout** moves books converted under the old naming, with a preview that lists every planned move before anything changes * Delete works on torrent-sourced books: it removes only the converted copy, and the torrent keeps seeding * Removed ingest books stay removed instead of reappearing on the next scan * The failed sign-in budget is global as well as per address, and IPv6 is counted per /64
### 0.18.0 * **Acquiring books**: a wishlist watcher searches your tracker and hands matches to qBittorrent, then converts whatever lands in the ingest folder. Off until configured * Wishlist is its own tab, with Discover to search the catalog and stored suggestions under the box * Watcher schedule, per-cycle limit and membership tier are editable in Settings > Watcher without a restart
### 0.15.1 * Every recommendation from the v0.15.0 security review is fixed: 1 high, 5 medium, 10 low and 3 info findings
### 0.15.0 * **Series - see what you are missing**: a Series tab counts the books you do not own, lists them, and lets you mark one you own without a rip * The library table fits the page down to a 1280px window
### 0.14.4 * Every finding from the v0.14.3 code audit is fixed: 4 high, 3 medium and 11 low * Cross-site requests are refused, ASINs are validated and cover downloads are allow-listed
### 0.14.0 * The conversion queue is visible: queued books leave the Review/Held lists and show in a "Waiting to convert" strip * Fixes from a full code audit, including books without a cover losing their tags and the auto-convert tier setting being ignored
Container.Description:
### What it does
Point Audiobind at a folder of audiobooks and a folder to write to. On a timer it:
1. **Groups parts into books** - `Book/Disc 1`, `Book/Part 2` and `Book/Part 10` become one book, not three. 2. **Verifies the book** against the Audible catalog: title, author, narrator, series, ASIN. 3. **Proves completeness** by comparing total runtime with the catalog runtime. A set that is an hour short is reported, not merged. 4. **Merges and converts**: one `.m4b`, AAC stereo at a 128 kbps floor (a richer source keeps its own bitrate; `AUDIO_CHANNELS=1` halves the file size), real chapter marks from Audnex, cover art and full tags embedded. 5. **Files it** as `Author/Book/Book.m4b` (or `Author/Series/3 - Title/Title.m4b`), with an Audiobookshelf-compatible `metadata.json`. Every author is in the folder, joined with ` & `.
### What it will not do
* Conversion never changes, moves or deletes your source files. Only the explicit Delete button in the web UI can remove a source folder (typed confirmation, no undo), and only while the library is mounted writable; set the library path to Read Only to rule even that out. * It does not convert anything it is unsure about. Matches that are only partial, or whose runtime disagrees with the catalog by more than 25%, are marked **review**/**held** on the status page for you to look at.
Suitable for Audiobookshelf, Plex, Emby, Jellyfin, Apple Books and anything else that reads standard m4b chapters and tags.

Config.Name: Library path
Config.Description: Folder holding the audiobooks to fix. Writable so Delete can fully remove a book. Owner decides: set Access Mode to Read Only for a guarantee the app never touches your sources - this disables source-delete (Delete then removes only the output).

Config.Name: Output path
Config.Description: Where finished m4b files are written. Never the same as the library path.

Config.Name: Appdata
Config.Description: Database, audit report and work files.

Config.Name: WebUI port
Config.Description: Status page and JSON API.

Config.Name: Allowed hosts
Config.Description: Comma-separated names/IPs you open the web UI with, e.g. 192.168.1.10,tower,tower.local. Any other address is refused (protects against DNS-rebinding attacks). Add your server's LAN IP here or the UI is only reachable from the server itself.

Config.Name: Access token
Config.Description: Only for upgrading: an install that still signs in with a token keeps working while this is set. On a new install leave it empty and create your account on the setup page that opens on the first visit - until you do, anyone who can reach this port can claim it, so finish setup right after the first start. Scripts send it as 'Authorization: Bearer TOKEN'.

Config.Name: Trusted proxy
Config.Description: true only when Audiobind sits behind your own reverse proxy: X-Forwarded-Host/-For/-Proto from the addresses in Trusted proxy IPs are then believed. Needs Trusted proxy IPs as well.

Config.Name: Trusted proxy IPs
Config.Description: Comma-separated addresses or CIDRs of your reverse proxy (for example 172.18.0.0/16). Forwarded headers are only honoured from these peers; empty means none.

Config.Name: Auto convert
Config.Description: Which confidence tiers convert without asking: high, medium or off.

Config.Name: Scan interval (minutes)
Config.Description: How often to look for new books.

Config.Name: Audio bitrate (floor)
Config.Description: Minimum AAC bitrate. A richer source keeps its own bitrate (a 256k mp3 stays 256k); anything below this is lifted to it. Capped at 320k.

Config.Name: Channels
Config.Description: 1 = mono, 2 = stereo. Stereo keeps the source layout; mono halves the file size.

Config.Name: Parallel jobs
Config.Description: Books converted at once. Raise if your CPU is idle.

Config.Name: Nice level
Config.Description: CPU priority for ffmpeg. Higher = yields to everything else.

Config.Name: Max runtime delta
Config.Description: Hold a book when its runtime differs from the catalog by more than this fraction (0.25 = 25%).

Config.Name: Region
Config.Description: Audible region for metadata: us, ca, uk, au, fr, de, it, es, jp, in.

Config.Name: Dry run
Config.Description: true = log every decision but write nothing.

Config.Name: Log file
Config.Description: Path of the rotating log file (5 MB, 3 backups). Written next to the console log, so it survives a container recreate. Set it to empty only if you want no file log.

Config.Name: Notify URL
Config.Description: Optional webhook (Discord/Slack/ntfy) posted a summary after each scan.

Config.Name: Ingest path
Config.Description: Optional. Folder where downloaded audiobooks land (for example qBittorrent's completed folder for the wishlist watcher). Mounted read-only. Leave empty to turn ingest off.

Config.Name: Ingest dir
Config.Description: Set to /ingest when the Ingest path above is used; empty = ingest off.

Config.Name: Tracker URL
Config.Description: Optional. Base URL of your private tracker, e.g. https://tracker.example (no path). The wishlist watcher is off until this, both paths, the cookie name and the session are set (plus the qBittorrent login below).

Config.Name: Tracker search path
Config.Description: Optional. Path of the tracker's JSON search endpoint.

Config.Name: Tracker search method
Config.Description: Optional. POST (default) or GET.

Config.Name: Tracker search category
Config.Description: Optional. The category value to send with a search, if the site needs one. Empty = none is sent.

Config.Name: Tracker search encoding
Config.Description: Optional. How a POST sends the search body: json (default) or form (application/x-www-form-urlencoded key=value pairs).

Config.Name: Tracker search body
Config.Description: Required for the watcher. The search request as a JSON object with {{title}}, {{author}} and {{category}} placeholders, e.g. {"q": "{{title}} {{author}}"}. A member that is only placeholders and comes out empty is left out.

Config.Name: Tracker download path
Config.Description: Optional. Path of the tracker's torrent download endpoint.

Config.Name: Tracker download id field
Config.Description: Optional. Query parameter carrying the torrent id (default tid).

Config.Name: Tracker freeleech field
Config.Description: Optional. Query parameter that spends a freeleech credit, e.g. fl. Empty = never sent.

Config.Name: Tracker cookie name
Config.Description: Optional. The name of the tracker's session cookie.

Config.Name: Tracker session (secret)
Config.Description: Optional. The value of the tracker's session cookie. Create the session for the IP the container reaches the tracker from. A secret.

Config.Name: Tracker proxy
Config.Description: Optional. http://host:port (or https://) proxy for every tracker request, e.g. a VPN container's HTTP proxy. Empty = direct. Fail-closed: a dead proxy means no tracker request, never a direct one. Prefer running Audiobind in the VPN container's network (see the README, Running the watcher through a VPN).

Config.Name: Tracker user agent
Config.Description: Optional. Text to send as the User-Agent to the tracker. Empty = audiobind/<version>. Set to none to send no User-Agent (some trackers refuse that with HTTP 400).

Config.Name: Tracker premium member
Config.Description: Set to true if your account holds the tracker's top membership tier. When false, torrents restricted to that tier are skipped instead of attempted. Can also be changed in Settings > Watcher without a restart.

Config.Name: Expected egress IP (guard)
Config.Description: Optional. Your VPN's exit address. When set, the watcher checks which IP the tracker would see before every cycle and refuses to contact it unless it is exactly this one. Leave empty to skip this check. Can also be changed in Settings > Watcher without a restart.

Config.Name: Home IP (guard)
Config.Description: Optional. Your home connection's public IP. When set, the watcher checks which IP the tracker would see before every cycle and refuses to contact it if it is this one, or if it cannot tell. One small HTTPS request per cycle to ipinfo.io.

Config.Name: Watcher dry run
Config.Description: true = the watcher searches and logs what it would download, but never downloads. Separate from Dry run.

Config.Name: Watch interval (minutes)
Config.Description: Minutes between wishlist watcher cycles (10-1440).

Config.Name: Watch max per cycle
Config.Description: Wanted books the watcher searches per cycle (1-20). Also editable in Settings > Watcher.

Config.Name: Watch max incomplete
Config.Description: No torrent is added in a cycle while this many in the qBittorrent category are still downloading. 0 = no limit.

Config.Name: qBittorrent URL
Config.Description: qBittorrent WebUI the watcher hands torrents to. If qBittorrent shares a VPN container's network with Audiobind, use http://127.0.0.1:8083 (the LAN address times out).

Config.Name: qBittorrent category
Config.Description: The qBittorrent category torrents are added to (its save path is your ingest folder).

Config.Name: qBittorrent user
Config.Description: qBittorrent WebUI username. The watcher stays disabled without a login.

Config.Name: qBittorrent password
Config.Description: qBittorrent WebUI password.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID for written files.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID for written files.

Config.Name: TZ
Config.Description: Timezone for log timestamps.
